intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC

selected_hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, dramatic limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart from Porto Vromi or Skinari Cape and include swimming stops in the crystal-clear Ionian Sea.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a guided food tour. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional Greek street food like souvlaki and spanakopita. Interact with local vendors and learn about Greek culinary traditions and ingredients that have been staples for centuries.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand created by crushed coral and shells. Wade through shallow lagoon waters to reach the small island of Elafonissi, snorkel in the warm Mediterranean waters, and relax on one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Rent a sunbed and umbrella for a full day of relaxation.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in a traditional Cretan home or local taverna. Learn to prepare authentic dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), and loukoumades (honey fritters). Visit a local olive oil producer beforehand to understand the foundation of Greek cuisine. Enjoy your creations with local wine or raki.

experiences.name: Sunset Dinner at a Oia Cliffside Taverna
experiences.description: Experience the world-famous Santorini sunset from the village of Oia while dining at a cliffside taverna. Savor fresh grilled octopus, fava (yellow split pea dip), tomatokeftedes (tomato fritters), and fresh catch of the day paired with local Assyrtiko white wine. The combination of spectacular caldera views, golden sunset light, and authentic Cycladic cuisine creates an unforgettable evening.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Zakynthos Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage and arrange transfer to Navagio Beach boutique stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the boutique stay near Navagio Beach. Once settled, take a short walk to the nearest viewpoint overlooking the iconic Navagio (Shipwreck) Beach for stunning first views. Relax and orient yourself with the local area.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearest village for a light first dinner. Explore the waterfront promenade and get a feel for the local pace of life.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Pick up a gyros wrap or tiropita (cheese pie) from a local bakery or kiosk near the accommodation for around €3–5.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a family-run taverna in the nearby village — try grilled octopus or moussaka with local house wine. Budget around €10–14 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Flight lands at 13:00; nothing is scheduled before arrival. Pre-book a shared shuttle or local bus from the airport to save on transfer costs (approx. €5–8 vs €30+ for a taxi). Exchange some euros at the airport if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the Navagio Beach viewpoint to catch the dramatic clifftop panorama before the crowds arrive. The turquoise cove and rusted shipwreck are best photographed in the morning light. Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat trip down to Navagio Beach itself — small group boat tours depart from Porto Vromi harbour (approx. €15–20 per person). Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise water and explore the famous shipwreck up close. Spend 2–3 hours on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village for sunset drinks at a clifftop café. Watch the sun dip into the Ionian Sea with a cold Mythos beer or fresh lemonade.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and fresh fruit from a local mini-market or bakery — budget €3–4.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic for the beach: bread, feta cheese, olives, tomatoes, and water from a local supermarket — budget €5–6.
meals.dinner: Taverna dinner with fresh grilled fish of the day, Greek salad, and bread. Look for daily specials on chalkboard menus — budget €12–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat trip in advance or at Porto Vromi harbour early morning to secure a spot. Wear reef-safe sunscreen. Navagio Beach has no facilities so bring everything you need.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Blue Caves on the northern tip of Zakynthos — another boat excursion from Agios Nikolaos port (approx. €15 per person). The sea caves reflect stunning blue light from the water below, best seen in morning calm conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the caves, relax at Makris Gialos or Alykanas Beach on the northeast coast. These are quieter, local-favourite beaches with free access and calm waters ideal for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local panigiri (village festival) if one is happening, or head to the village square for an evening ouzo and meze spread at a traditional kafeneion (café-bar).

meals.breakfast: Spanakopita (spinach pie) and Greek coffee from a local bakery — budget €3.
meals.lunch: Souvlaki plate with pita, tzatziki, and salad from a local grill house — budget €7–9.
meals.dinner: Meze dinner: order a spread of small dishes like taramosalata, dolmades, grilled halloumi, and saganaki to share. Budget €10–13 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Caves are best visited in the morning when the light penetration is most vivid. Wear a hat and bring a light layer for the boat ride. Check local village noticeboards for any evening events or festivals.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or use the local bus to explore the Zakynthos interior. Visit the hillside village of Keri for panoramic sea views and traditional Zakynthian architecture. Stop at the Keri lighthouse for sweeping views of the southern coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Keri Beach — a small, pebbly cove surrounded by pine-covered cliffs. Swim and snorkel in the clear waters. This is a quieter, more local beach away from the tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the main village area. Visit the local weekly market if available, or browse small shops for local products like Zakynthian honey, olive oil, and mandolato nougat.

meals.breakfast: Home-style breakfast at the boutique stay if included, or pick up a bougatsa (custard pastry) and coffee — budget €3–4.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a simple village taverna in Keri — try lamb kleftiko or stuffed tomatoes (gemista). Budget €8–11.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using local market produce (pasta, fresh vegetables, local cheese) to save money, or grab a budget souvlaki — budget €5–8.

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental typically costs €15–25 per day; always wear a helmet. Alternatively, local buses run limited routes — check schedules in advance. Keri lighthouse area can be windy even on hot days.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Zakynthos Town (Zante Town) by local bus or shared taxi. Visit the Museum of Solomos and Eminent Zakynthians (€3 entry) to learn about the island's cultural heritage and the poet Dionysios Solomos who wrote the Greek national anthem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Zakynthos Town on foot: walk through Plateia Agiou Markou (Saint Mark's Square), visit the Byzantine Museum (€3), and browse the Venetian-era architecture. Stroll along the harbour waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely dinner in Zakynthos Town before the bus back. The town has a wider variety of affordable restaurants and street food options than the Navagio area.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and koulouri (sesame bread ring) from a street vendor in Zakynthos Town — budget €2.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a harbour-side restaurant — try fresh calamari or shrimp pasta with a glass of local white wine. Budget €10–13.
meals.dinner: Traditional Zakynthian stifado (slow-cooked meat stew) at a side-street taverna away from the main tourist strip. Budget €9–12.

day_by_day.notes: Local buses to Zakynthos Town run several times daily and cost around €2–3 each way. The town is largely a pedestrian-friendly area. The Byzantine Museum houses important post-Byzantine icons rescued from earthquake-damaged churches.

day_by_day.morning: Relax morning at the beach closest to the boutique stay. Swim, read, and soak up the sun. Collect sea glass or shells along the shoreline for a slow, peaceful start to the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Laganas area to see the loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta) nesting beaches. Join a free guided walk organised by the Sea Turtle Protection Society (ARCHELON) to learn about conservation efforts — free or donation-based.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset swim at a quiet cove near the accommodation. Many small unnamed coves along the Zakynthos coastline are accessible on foot and completely free.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with local honey and walnuts prepared at the accommodation — budget €3–4 from supermarket supplies.
meals.lunch: Gyros wrap with tzatziki and chips from a local takeaway — budget €4–5.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local taverna — try briam (Greek ratatouille) and grilled chicken with lemon potatoes, a classic budget-friendly combo. Budget €9–12.

day_by_day.notes: Laganas beach is a protected nesting area — do not disturb the sand, use lights, or approach turtles. ARCHELON volunteers are usually present in the evenings near the beach. Turtle sightings are common in the water during June.

day_by_day.morning: Ferry from Zakynthos to Killini on the Peloponnese mainland (approx. €8–10, 1.5 hours). From Killini, take a bus or shared taxi to Patras — the gateway to the broader Peloponnese region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Patras. Visit the imposing Patras Castle (Kastro) perched on a hill above the city — free entry. Enjoy panoramic views of the Gulf of Patras and the Rio-Antirrio Bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Patras' lively city centre. The city is known for its vibrant street life and café culture. Walk along the waterfront promenade and enjoy the evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the ferry — bread, cheese, and fruit from the accommodation. Budget €3.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Patras at a city centre eatery — try a hearty bean soup (fasolada) or lentil soup (fakes), traditional Greek staples. Budget €6–8.
meals.dinner: Patras is known for its excellent local food scene. Dinner at a mezedopoleion (meze restaurant) — order a selection of small plates to share. Budget €10–13.

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules in advance as times vary. Book the ferry online to save time at the port. Patras is a transit hub — accommodation here is generally affordable. Consider a budget hostel or guesthouse for €20–35 per night.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip from Patras to Ancient Olympia by bus (approx. 1.5–2 hours, €8–10 each way). Visit the Archaeological Site of Olympia — birthplace of the Olympic Games. Walk through the Temple of Zeus ruins, the ancient stadium, and the Palaistra wrestling school.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the excellent Museum of the History of the Olympic Games in Antiquity (combined ticket with site approx. €12). See the famous statue of Hermes by Praxiteles and the Nike of Paionios. Allow 2–3 hours for the museum.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Patras by bus. Enjoy a relaxed evening meal and early rest after a full day of sightseeing.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and tiropita from a Patras bakery before the bus — budget €3.
meals.lunch: Lunch near Olympia village — simple taverna meal of grilled pork chops (brizoles) with salad and bread. Budget €9–11.
meals.dinner: Simple souvlaki dinner near the Patras accommodation — budget €6–8.

day_by_day.notes: Ancient Olympia is one of Greece's most significant archaeological sites. Visit early to avoid peak heat (temperatures can exceed 35°C inland in June). Bring a hat, sunscreen, and plenty of water. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Patras to Athens by intercity bus (KTEL) — approximately 3 hours, €20–22. Arrive at Athens' Kifissos bus terminal and transfer to central Athens by metro or taxi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to budget accommodation in Athens (Monastiraki or Psiri neighbourhood recommended for location and value — €20–40/night for a hostel or budget guesthouse). Explore Monastiraki flea market and the lively Psiri district on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Walk up to the Acropolis Hill for the free sunset view from below (the Acropolis itself closes at 8 PM but the surrounding area and Filopappou Hill are free). Watch the city light up as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast on the bus or at the Patras terminal — koulouri and coffee, budget €3.
meals.lunch: Street food lunch in Monastiraki — souvlaki from the famous Thanasis or Bairaktaris restaurants, budget €5–7.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Psiri neighbourhood — try a traditional Greek taverna with live rembetiko music some evenings. Budget €10–13.

day_by_day.notes: The KTEL bus from Patras is comfortable and reliable — book tickets online in advance. Athens' metro system is efficient and affordable (€1.20 per journey). The Monastiraki area is central, lively, and budget-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis of Athens — book tickets online in advance to avoid queues (€20 standard, or €10 reduced). See the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Arrive at opening time (8 AM) to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis Museum (€10 entry) at the base of the hill — one of Europe's finest modern museums, housing original Parthenon sculptures and artefacts from the Acropolis site. Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Plaka neighbourhood — Athens' oldest district with charming neoclassical streets, bougainvillea-draped houses, and souvenir shops. Enjoy dinner in one of the neighbourhood's many tavernas.

meals.breakfast: Greek breakfast at a café near the accommodation — eggs, olives, tomato, feta, and bread. Budget €5–7.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at a traditional ouzeri near the Acropolis Museum — mezedes and cold beer. Budget €8–10.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Plaka — try pastitsio (Greek lasagne) or roast lamb at a family taverna. Budget €11–14.

day_by_day.notes: The Acropolis is the highlight of any Greece trip — go early to avoid the midday heat (29°C+ in June). The combined ticket covers multiple archaeological sites in Athens. Wear sturdy non-slip shoes as the marble surfaces can be slippery.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Archaeological Museum (€10 entry) — the largest archaeological museum in Greece, housing treasures from across the country including the Antikythera Mechanism and Mycenaean gold masks. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Athens Central Market (Varvakios Agora) — a bustling indoor market full of fresh fish, meat, spices, olives, and local produce. A sensory feast and a great place to pick up affordable local snacks. Afterwards, wander through Omonia and Exarchia neighbourhoods.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gazi or Thissio neighbourhood for the evening — these areas have rooftop bars with Acropolis views. Enjoy a sunset cocktail or local wine at a rooftop café before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Bougatsa (cream-filled pastry) and Greek coffee at a local zacharoplasteion (patisserie) — budget €3–4.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Central Market area — fresh seafood or a hearty bowl of offal soup (patsas) if adventurous, or a simple salad and bread. Budget €7–9.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Thissio with Acropolis views — look for restaurants on Apostolou Pavlou street. Budget €12–15.

day_by_day.notes: The Athens Central Market is closed on Sundays. The National Archaeological Museum is one of the world's great museums — don't rush it. Exarchia is a bohemian neighbourhood known for independent bookshops, street art, and cheap cafés.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Piraeus port and catch a ferry to the island of Aegina (approx. €8–9 each way, 40 minutes by fast ferry). Aegina is a perfect budget day-trip island — close, affordable, and less crowded than the Cyclades.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or take a local bus to the Temple of Aphaia (€6 entry) — a remarkably well-preserved ancient temple with panoramic sea views. Afterwards, head to Agia Marina beach for a swim in the clear Saronic Gulf waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Piraeus by ferry and head back to Athens. Spend the final evening in Athens enjoying dinner and a leisurely walk through the illuminated Plaka and Monastiraki districts.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast near Piraeus port — coffee and a cheese pie from a port-side bakery. Budget €3.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Aegina town — the island is famous for its pistachios and fresh seafood. Try grilled red mullet (barbounia) at a harbour taverna. Budget €10–13.
meals.dinner: Final Athens dinner — splurge slightly on a nicer mezedopoleion with a wider meze spread and local wine. Budget €14–18.

day_by_day.notes: Aegina is one of the most accessible and affordable Greek islands from Athens. Buy a return ferry ticket at Piraeus port. Bicycle rental in Aegina costs around €5–8 for the day. The island's pistachios make great affordable souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — revisit a favourite spot or explore anything missed. Visit the free Syntagma Square and watch the Evzone guards change at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier (change occurs on the hour). Browse last-minute souvenirs at Monastiraki.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, head to Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) by metro (€9 from city centre, 40 minutes). Check in and complete departure procedures.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Athens. Reflect on 13 wonderful days exploring the beaches, history, and local food of Greece.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — a proper sit-down meal of eggs, feta, olives, tomatoes, and fresh bread at a neighbourhood café. Budget €6–8.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Syntagma or at the airport — a wrap or salad. Budget €6–9.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for Athens airport check-in. The metro to the airport runs frequently and is the most budget-friendly option (€9). Keep some euros for airport purchases. Final budget tip: pack any leftover local snacks (olives, honey, pistachios) in your checked luggage as edible souvenirs.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from airport to Navagio Beach boutique hotel (approx. 1–1.5 hrs including ferry crossing to Zakynthos). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the local area near your accommodation to get your bearings. Enjoy the stunning clifftop views of the Ionian Sea near Navagio.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a nearby taverna in the Anafonitria or Volimes village area for a relaxed welcome dinner. Try local Zakynthian specialties such as sofrito (beef in white wine sauce) or fresh grilled fish.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a snack stop during transfer
meals.dinner: Taverna Navagio or a local family-run taverna near Anafonitria village — budget €15–25 per person for a full meal with local wine

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light and relaxed. The ferry crossing from the mainland port (if flying into Patras/Kyllini area) or a short domestic connection via Zakynthos Airport is required. Confirm transfer arrangements in advance. Hydrate well after travel.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) by boat tour — book a morning excursion from Porto Vromi or Agios Nikolaos port. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters and photograph the famous MV Panagiotis shipwreck nestled in the white pebble cove.
day_by_day.afternoon: After returning from the boat tour, explore the Blue Caves along the northern coast — often included in combined boat tours. The sea caves glow brilliant blue from light refraction and are perfect for snorkeling. Return to hotel for a midday rest during peak heat.
day_by_day.evening: Drive or take a taxi to Volimes village, the largest village in northern Zakynthos. Browse local honey, nougat (mandolato), and handmade lace shops before settling in for dinner at a village square restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery — fresh tiropita (cheese pie) and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a seaside café near Porto Vromi after the boat tour — grilled octopus, Greek salad, and bread €12–18
meals.dinner: Taverna in Volimes village square — try lamb kleftiko or local pastitsada with a carafe of house wine €18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Navagio + Blue Caves boat tour in advance, especially in June. Morning departures (around 9:00–10:00) are best to beat crowds and afternoon winds. Wear reef-safe sunscreen and bring water shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a car or scooter for the day and drive south to Zakynthos Town (Chora). Explore the Venetian-influenced town center, visit the Byzantine Museum on Solomos Square, and walk through the ruins of Zakynthos Castle (Bochali Hill) for panoramic views over the town and bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south to the famous Gerakas Beach, a protected loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta) nesting site. Swim in the calm, shallow turquoise waters and keep an eye out for turtles. Nearby Dafni Beach is another quiet option. Note beach rules protecting turtle nests.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Zakynthos Town for dinner in the harbor area. Explore the lively waterfront promenade (Lombardou Street) and dine at a mid-range seafood restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café in Anafonitria — Greek yogurt with thyme honey and walnuts
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar near Gerakas — sandwiches, fresh juice, and loukoumades (honey doughnuts) €8–12
meals.dinner: Seafood restaurant on Zakynthos Town harbor — grilled sea bream, tzatziki, and village salad with local Robola wine €20–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Gerakas Beach has restricted hours (open until 19:30) to protect nesting turtles. Do not disturb any marked nests or approach turtles. Car rental from local agencies costs approximately €35–50/day.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the western coast — drive to Porto Limnionas, a stunning natural rocky inlet perfect for snorkeling in clear deep-blue water. Bring snorkeling gear (rentable locally) and explore the underwater rock formations and fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kampi, a clifftop village on the western coast famous for its dramatic sunset views over the Ionian Sea. Visit the large cross monument at the cliff edge. Relax at a clifftop café and enjoy the scenery. Then swing by Exo Chora village to see traditional Zakynthian architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the northern area near your hotel. Enjoy a quiet evening dining at a local taverna in Anafonitria — one of the most authentic and uncrowded spots on the island.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local bakery — spanakopita and freddo espresso
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a local mini-market — local cheese, olives, bread, tomatoes, and cold cuts eaten at Porto Limnionas €8–10
meals.dinner: Taverna Anafonitria — homestyle moussaka, horta (wild greens), and local bread with olive oil €15–20 per person

day_by_day.notes: Porto Limnionas has no lifeguard — swim with care. The rocky entry requires water shoes. Kampi is best visited late afternoon for optimal sunset light (sunset around 20:45 in June).

day_by_day.morning: Take a full-day ferry from Zakynthos to Kefalonia (Poros or Argostoli port — approx. 1.5–2.5 hrs depending on route). Check into a mid-range hotel or guesthouse in Argostoli, the island capital. Walk around the lively Lithostroto pedestrian street and the De Bosset Bridge (longest stone bridge in the world over sea water).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Melissani Lake Cave — a stunning underground lake with a collapsed roof that allows sunlight to filter in, turning the water an ethereal blue. Boat rides inside the cave are included in the entrance fee. Then stop at Drogarati Cave nearby, a vast stalactite cavern with remarkable acoustics.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Argostoli town center. The main square (Plateia Valianou) buzzes with life in the evenings. Explore the local restaurants and try Kefalonian meat pie (kreatopita) and local Robola white wine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café in Argostoli after arrival
meals.lunch: Café or taverna near Melissani Lake — souvlaki wrap and Greek salad €10–15
meals.dinner: Restaurant on Argostoli waterfront or main square — Kefalonian kreatopita, fresh mussels saganaki, and Robola wine €20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Zakynthos–Kefalonia ferry in advance via ionian-pelagos.gr or local ferry operators. Melissani Cave can be crowded midday — aim for late morning or early afternoon visit. Entrance to Melissani is approximately €8, Drogarati €5.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Myrtos Beach — consistently ranked among the most beautiful beaches in Greece and Europe. Arrive early (before 10:00) to secure a good spot. The beach features dramatic white pebbles, towering limestone cliffs, and strikingly vivid turquoise water. Swim and relax.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north to Assos village — a picturesque peninsula village with pastel-colored houses and a Venetian castle. Walk up to the castle ruins for sweeping views of the turquoise bay below. Swim at the small pebbly beach in the village cove.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Fiskardo, the only village on Kefalonia that survived the 1953 earthquake, preserving its original Venetian architecture. Stroll the harbor lined with yachts and colorful buildings, then dine at one of the waterfront restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a bakery in Argostoli before departing
meals.lunch: Taverna at Assos village — fresh fish of the day, village salad, and local bread €15–22
meals.dinner: Waterfront restaurant in Fiskardo — grilled lobster pasta or fresh catch of the day with local wine €25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Myrtos Beach has limited shade and strong afternoon waves — bring an umbrella and be cautious swimming if waves are high. The road down to Myrtos is steep and winding; drive carefully. Fiskardo is upscale — budget slightly more for dinner here.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Antisamos Beach on the eastern coast of Kefalonia — a lush green hillside-backed pebble beach made famous by the film 'Captain Corelli's Mandolin.' Crystal-clear calm water ideal for snorkeling. Enjoy a relaxed morning swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the village of Sami nearby and visit the ancient ruins of the Acropolis of Sami. Then head to the Archaeological Museum of Argostoli (open until 15:00) for a cultural afternoon learning about the island's rich history from Mycenaean times through the Venetian era.
day_by_day.evening: Last evening in Kefalonia — enjoy a sunset walk along the Argostoli waterfront where loggerhead sea turtles often surface near the port. Dine at a mid-range restaurant in Argostoli for a farewell Kefalonian meal.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Antisamos or Sami waterfront — grilled calamari, tzatziki, and cold Mythos beer €12–18
meals.dinner: Taverna in Argostoli — stuffed peppers with rice and minced meat, dakos salad, and local wine €18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Antisamos Beach is a 15-minute drive from Sami. The Archaeological Museum of Argostoli charges approximately €4 entry. Book your ferry back to Zakynthos or onward to Corfu/Athens for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Return ferry from Kefalonia back to Zakynthos (morning departure). Check back into your Navagio Beach boutique hotel. Spend the late morning relaxing and recovering from travel with a swim at a nearby beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Xigia Beach on the northeastern coast — a unique beach with natural sulfur springs bubbling up from the seabed, believed to have therapeutic properties. The water has a slightly warm, mineral-rich quality. Snorkel and enjoy the unusual experience.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening near your hotel. Visit a local wine producer in the Volimes area — Zakynthos produces excellent local wines including Verdea. Many small wineries offer informal tastings. Dinner at a local taverna.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before ferry departure — café near port or hotel
meals.lunch: Snack bar or packed lunch at Xigia Beach — sandwiches and fresh fruit €8–10
meals.dinner: Local taverna near Navagio area — grilled lamb chops, horiatiki salad, and Verdea wine €18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Xigia Beach has a strong sulfur smell from the springs — this is normal and temporary. The beach is pebbly and the springs are strongest near the cliff face. Bring water shoes. Wine tastings at small local producers are often free or very low cost (€5–10) with advance arrangement.

day_by_day.morning: Take a cooking class or food experience in Zakynthos — many local families and small operators offer half-day sessions teaching traditional Zakynthian recipes such as sofrito, mandolato, and local pastries. Book in advance through your hotel or local tourism offices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Laganas Bay area on the southern coast — the heart of the National Marine Park of Zakynthos. Walk along the long sandy beach (one of the longest in Greece) and learn about the sea turtle conservation program at the information center near Laganas. Swim in the calm shallow bay.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Zakynthos Town for a final time — visit the Solomos Museum dedicated to Dionysios Solomos, author of the Greek national anthem (a native of Zakynthos). Then enjoy dinner at a rooftop restaurant overlooking the town.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Light lunch included in cooking class or a taverna in Laganas €12–18
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant in Zakynthos Town — grilled sea bass, stuffed zucchini flowers, and local rosé wine €22–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Laganas Beach has strict rules protecting turtle nesting sites — stay on designated areas and never use artificial lights at night near the beach. Cooking classes typically cost €45–65 per person and are a wonderful cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak or join a guided sea kayaking tour along the dramatic northern coastline near Navagio. Paddle through sea caves, under towering limestone cliffs, and into hidden coves inaccessible by land. A spectacular and active way to experience the island's coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return and relax at your boutique hotel. Enjoy the pool or a quiet afternoon at a nearby secluded beach. Read, nap, and recharge — a perfect balanced-trip afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from the clifftop lookout above Navagio Beach — one of the most photographed viewpoints in Greece. The late afternoon light over the shipwreck is extraordinary. Then dinner at a nearby taverna to close out the evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Post-kayak snack at a Porto Vromi café — fresh orange juice, cheese pie, and fruit €8–12
meals.dinner: Taverna near Anafonitria — mixed seafood platter, village salad, and local wine €20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Guided sea kayaking tours from Porto Vromi cost approximately €35–55 per person for a half-day. Wear water shoes and reef-safe sunscreen. The Navagio viewpoint is accessible by car/scooter — arrive 30–45 minutes before sunset for the best light and to secure a spot.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a final leisurely morning at Navagio Beach or one of the nearby northern beaches such as Makris Gialos. Simply swim, snorkel, and soak in the beautiful Ionian scenery. This is your last full beach day — make the most of it.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monastery of Anafonitria — the oldest monastery on Zakynthos (15th century), located just minutes from your hotel. The monastery is where Saint Dionysios (patron saint of Zakynthos) lived as a monk. A peaceful, historically rich visit. Then browse the village of Anafonitria for local honey and handicrafts to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner at the best local restaurant you've discovered during your stay, or try a new spot recommended by your hotel. Celebrate the trip with a full traditional Zakynthian feast.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy it slowly, no rush today
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Makris Gialos or packed picnic — local cheese, olives, bread, and cold cuts €10–15
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a recommended taverna — full spread of mezedes (dips, dolmades, grilled vegetables), main fish or meat dish, dessert, and wine €25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Monastery of Anafonitria is free to enter but dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered — scarves available at the entrance). Opening hours are typically 8:00–13:00 and 17:00–20:00. Confirm locally.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning swim and breakfast at the hotel. Pack and check out. If time allows before transfer, take one last clifftop walk above Navagio for a final view of the iconic shipwreck beach — a memory to last a lifetime.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Zakynthos Airport or port for onward travel. If your departure is late afternoon or evening, store luggage at the hotel and spend a few final hours in Zakynthos Town — pick up last-minute souvenirs such as local olive oil, mandolato nougat, honey, or Verdea wine.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Zakynthos or overnight in Zakynthos Town if flight is the following morning. If staying, enjoy a simple dinner near the port.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — enjoy Greek yogurt, honey, fresh fruit, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Zakynthos Town before departure — souvlaki wrap or a gyros from a local grill shop €6–10
meals.dinner: Airport lounge snack or a simple waterfront café dinner if staying overnight €12–18

day_by_day.notes: Zakynthos Airport (ZTH) is approximately 35–40 minutes from Navagio area. Allow extra time for luggage and check-in. Confirm your return flight details and any ferry connections. Great souvenir shops are found on Lithostroto pedestrian street in Zakynthos Town.

day_by_day.morning: If overnight in Zakynthos Town: enjoy a final Greek breakfast at a harbor café — fresh bread, local butter and honey, hard-boiled eggs, and a strong freddo cappuccino. Take a final walk along the waterfront and watch the fishing boats return with the morning catch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final departure from Zakynthos. Reflect on 13 incredible days of turquoise waters, fresh seafood, golden sunsets, and warm Greek hospitality. Safe travels home.
day_by_day.evening: In transit or arrived home

meals.breakfast: Harbor café in Zakynthos Town — full Greek breakfast spread €8–12
meals.lunch: Airport or in-flight
meals.dinner: In transit or at home

day_by_day.notes: This final day serves as a buffer for late departures or any travel delays. Greece's islands can have ferry and flight schedule changes — always have a flexible plan. Consider leaving a review for your boutique hotel and any standout tavernas to help other travelers discover these gems.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Zakynthos International Airport at 13:00. Private luxury transfer arranged to your boutique stay at Navagio Beach. Check in, settle into your suite, and enjoy a welcome drink on your private terrace overlooking the Ionian Sea. Take a leisurely stroll along the clifftops above Navagio Beach to soak in your first breathtaking views of the iconic Shipwreck Beach.
day_by_day.evening: Unwind with a sunset aperitivo on the terrace of your boutique hotel. Enjoy the golden-hour light over the turquoise coves before heading to dinner at a nearby clifftop restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Enjoyed on the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Light mezze platter and fresh juice at the hotel upon arrival – chilled watermelon, olives, local cheeses, and prosciutto-style cured meats served by the pool
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nobelos Clifftop Restaurant (or similar premium clifftop venue near Navagio) – grilled fresh catch of the day, Zakynthian salad with local capers, and a bottle of Assyrtiko white wine from Santorini

day_by_day.notes: Arrange your private airport transfer in advance through the hotel concierge. Navagio Beach area is remote – stock up on any essentials in Zakynthos Town if needed. Sunset from the Navagio viewpoint is approximately 20:45 in mid-June.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a private sunrise viewing at the Navagio (Shipwreck) Beach clifftop viewpoint – one of the most photographed spots in Greece. The morning light on the turquoise lagoon and the rusted wreck of the Panagiotis is extraordinary. Arrange a private boat charter from the hotel to descend to Navagio Beach itself – accessible only by sea – for an exclusive morning swim before the day-tripper crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue your private boat tour along the dramatic northern Zakynthos coastline, exploring the famous Blue Caves near Cape Skinari. Snorkel in the electric-blue waters inside the sea caves, where refracted sunlight creates an otherworldly azure glow. Return to the hotel for a poolside lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a private in-suite dining experience or dine at the hotel's signature restaurant. Watch the stars emerge over the Ionian Sea from your terrace with a glass of local Verdea wine.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet Greek breakfast at the hotel – fresh-baked spanakopita, local honey and thyme yogurt, seasonal fruit platter, Freddo espresso, and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Poolside mezze lunch at the hotel – grilled octopus drizzled with olive oil and lemon, tzatziki, warm pita, and a chilled rosé from the Peloponnese
meals.dinner: Premium in-hotel dining – slow-roasted lamb with rosemary and lemon potatoes, dakos salad with Cretan barley rusk, feta, and heirloom tomatoes, finished with loukoumades (honey doughnuts) and vanilla ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Book your private boat charter at least 24 hours in advance through the hotel concierge. Depart for Navagio Beach by boat no later than 08:00 to beat the tour boats. Apply high-SPF sunscreen – UV index is extreme in mid-June. Bring water shoes for the cave snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided jeep or ATV tour of the rugged northern Zakynthos highlands. Explore the medieval village of Volimes, famous for its traditional honey, handmade lace, and local ceramics. Visit a family-run olive oil producer for a private tasting and tour of their ancient groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Porto Vromi Bay – a secluded pebble cove near Navagio accessible by a dramatic cliff road. Swim in the crystal-clear waters and relax on a sun lounger with a private beach setup arranged by your hotel. Alternatively, take a short boat ride from Porto Vromi to explore hidden sea caves and secluded coves inaccessible by land.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a pre-dinner spa treatment (book a traditional Greek olive oil massage or a sea-salt scrub at the hotel spa). Dress for a premium dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast on your private terrace – Greek yogurt with Zakynthian thyme honey, smoked salmon on sourdough, soft-boiled eggs, and a fresh fruit bowl
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch basket prepared by the hotel chef and enjoyed at Porto Vromi Bay – artisan sandwiches, local cheese, cured meats, fresh fruit, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Arekia Traditional Taverna in Volimes (or similar premium village taverna) – slow-cooked kokkinisto beef stifado, village-style roasted vegetables, fresh bread, and local barrel wine

day_by_day.notes: The road to Porto Vromi is steep and narrow – a 4WD vehicle or guided jeep tour is strongly recommended. Volimes village shops typically close between 14:00–17:00 for siesta. The olive oil tasting experience should be booked through the hotel concierge in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury yacht day begins. Depart from Porto Vromi or the nearest marina on a full-day private yacht charter around Zakynthos. Start with a morning cruise south along the west coast, stopping at the secluded Marathonisi (Turtle Island) – a protected Caretta caretta sea turtle nesting site. Snorkel in the turquoise shallows and, if lucky, spot sea turtles in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the yacht journey to the Keri Caves and Keri Lagoon on the southern tip of Zakynthos. Swim through dramatic sea arches and natural rock formations. The yacht crew will prepare a gourmet onboard lunch as you anchor in a private cove. Sunbathe on the deck with the Ionian Sea all to yourselves.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the marina by late afternoon. Freshen up at the hotel and head to Zakynthos Town (Chora) for an evening of exploration and premium dining.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at the hotel before departure – pastries, fruit, coffee, and juice
meals.lunch: Gourmet onboard yacht lunch prepared by the crew – fresh grilled sea bream, Greek salad, chilled seafood platter, crusty bread, and chilled Assyrtiko wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malanos Restaurant in Zakynthos Town – one of the island's most celebrated traditional restaurants. Try the Zakynthian rabbit stifado, fresh pasta with local seafood, and the house barrel white wine

day_by_day.notes: Full-day private yacht charters in Zakynthos typically cost €600–€1,200+ depending on yacht size. Book at least 3 days in advance. Bring biodegradable sunscreen to protect the marine ecosystem around Marathonisi. Zakynthos Town is approximately 35–40 minutes by car from Navagio Beach area.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the hotel. Enjoy a slow breakfast followed by a private yoga session on the clifftop terrace arranged by the hotel (book through concierge). Spend time reading, journaling, or simply gazing at the Ionian Sea from your suite balcony.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the secluded Xigia Beach on the northeast coast of Zakynthos – a unique beach with natural sulphur springs bubbling up from the seabed, believed to have therapeutic properties. The water has a distinctive warm, silky quality. Swim and float in this natural spa-like sea environment. The beach is backed by dramatic white cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for sunset cocktails at the clifftop bar. Enjoy a premium tasting menu dinner at the hotel restaurant with wine pairing.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury breakfast at the hotel – eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh pastries, a full Greek spread of cheeses, olives, and cured meats, plus freshly brewed filter coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside café near Xigia Beach – grilled calamari, horiatiki salad, and a cold Mythos beer or fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Hotel tasting menu with wine pairing – a curated 5-course menu featuring the best of Ionian and Greek cuisine: zucchini blossoms stuffed with ricotta, prawn saganaki, sea bass carpaccio, lamb chops with mint sauce, and baklava semifreddo for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Xigia Beach has limited facilities – bring your own towels and water. The sulphur smell is noticeable but the water is refreshing and therapeutic. The beach is best visited on weekday mornings or early afternoons to avoid crowds. Wear old swimwear as the sulphur can discolour fabric.

day_by_day.morning: Private food and culture tour of Zakynthos Town (Chora). Begin with a guided walk through the historic Venetian-era town, visiting the Byzantine Museum with its remarkable collection of rescued post-Byzantine icons and frescoes. Explore the elegant Plateia Solomou (Solomon's Square) and the neoclassical architecture rebuilt after the 1953 earthquake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided visit to a local Zakynthian winery – the island produces the rare indigenous Verdea white wine. Enjoy a private cellar tour and premium wine tasting paired with local charcuterie, cheeses, and honey. Afterwards, browse the artisan shops of Zakynthos Town for local specialties: Mandolato nougat, Pasteli sesame bars, and Zakynthian olive oil.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at the rooftop bar of a luxury hotel in Zakynthos Town with panoramic views of the harbour and Peloponnese coastline. Dinner at one of the town's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Grab-and-go breakfast from the hotel before departure – fresh pastries, yogurt cups, and coffee
meals.lunch: Winery lunch pairing – artisan bread, aged local cheeses, fig jam, cured meats, olives, and a full Verdea wine tasting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Zakanthi Restaurant in Zakynthos Town – celebrated for its refined take on traditional Ionian cuisine. Try the Bianco (white fish stew with garlic and pepper), lobster pasta, and fresh grilled fish priced by weight

day_by_day.notes: The Byzantine Museum in Zakynthos Town is closed on Mondays – verify opening hours. Arrange a private guide through the hotel for the town walking tour. Zakynthian Verdea wine is rarely exported – purchase bottles directly from the winery to take home. The drive back to Navagio from Zakynthos Town at night requires care on mountain roads.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and relaxation day at the hotel. Spend the morning at the hotel pool or private beach access point. Indulge in a 90-minute couples' or solo spa treatment – choose from a traditional Greek olive oil and herb massage, a Thalasso sea therapy treatment, or a deep-tissue sports massage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private paddleboarding or sea kayaking session along the coastline near Navagio, guided by a local water sports instructor. Explore hidden coves and sea arches only accessible by paddleboard or kayak. Return to the hotel for a late afternoon swim and poolside relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachside dinner experience arranged by the hotel on a secluded cove below the cliffs – white-linen table for two (or your group), torchlit setting, personal chef, and sommelier. One of the most romantic and memorable experiences in Zakynthos.

meals.breakfast: Room service breakfast in bed – full Greek spread delivered to your suite with fresh flowers and a newspaper
meals.lunch: Poolside light lunch – avocado and prawn salad, chilled gazpacho, artisan sourdough, and a glass of chilled Rosé
meals.dinner: Private beachside dinner – freshly caught lobster thermidor, hand-dived scallops, truffle risotto, and a premium Greek wine selection curated by the hotel sommelier. Dessert: fresh fruit pavlova with Ionian honey

day_by_day.notes: The private beachside dinner experience must be booked at least 48 hours in advance and is weather-dependent. Cost is typically €200–€400 per person including wine pairing. This is the midpoint of your trip – a perfect day to recharge before the second half of your journey.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Strofades Islands – a remote uninhabited island group about 37 nautical miles south of Zakynthos, accessible only by private boat charter. These protected islands are a UNESCO-designated wetland and a critical stopover for migratory birds. Visit the Byzantine monastery of Pantokrator, one of the oldest in Greece, and walk the wild, untouched beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim and snorkel in the pristine, completely undeveloped waters around the Strofades. The sea here is exceptionally clear and rich with marine life. Enjoy a gourmet onboard lunch as you anchor in the calm waters. Begin the return journey to Zakynthos in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at the hotel by early evening. Freshen up and enjoy a quiet dinner at the hotel or a nearby clifftop restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure – Greek yogurt, honey, nuts, fruit, and strong espresso
meals.lunch: Gourmet onboard lunch on the charter boat – fresh seafood mezze, cold cuts, salads, fruit, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Relaxed dinner at the hotel restaurant – simple and fresh: grilled whole sea bass with lemon and herbs, roasted vegetables, and a light dessert of fresh fruit sorbet

day_by_day.notes: The Strofades day trip is a full-day excursion (approximately 10–12 hours). The crossing can be rough in strong winds – check weather forecasts carefully. This trip requires a larger private vessel (not a small speedboat). Bring motion sickness medication if needed. The monastery may have restricted visiting hours – confirm in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class at a local Zakynthian family home or premium culinary studio. Learn to prepare traditional Ionian dishes from scratch: sofrito (veal in white wine and garlic sauce), pastitsada, fresh spanakopita, and loukoumades. Your instructor will take you to the local morning market first to select the freshest ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sit down to enjoy the lunch you have prepared together. Afterwards, visit a local producer of Zakynthian olive oil and honey for a guided tasting. Spend the late afternoon at leisure – perhaps a final swim at Navagio Beach or relaxation at the hotel pool.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the hotel clifftop bar, followed by a premium dinner at one of Zakynthos's finest dining establishments.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – full spread of Greek specialties, fresh pastries, eggs to order, and coffee
meals.lunch: The dishes you prepared during your cooking class – sofrito, spanakopita, Greek salad, and loukoumades with honey for dessert, paired with local wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Buongiorno Restaurant or a comparable premium venue – Ionian-Italian fusion cuisine: fresh pasta with sea urchin, grilled lobster, tiramisu with a Greek twist using mastiha liqueur

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class should be arranged through the hotel concierge and typically costs €80–€150 per person. The market visit begins around 08:00 when produce is freshest. This is a wonderful way to take a piece of Zakynthian culinary culture home with you.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hike along the clifftop trail above Navagio Beach – one of the most dramatic coastal walks in Greece. The path offers jaw-dropping aerial views of the Shipwreck Beach lagoon in the early morning light. Bring a camera for the golden-hour photography. The hike is moderate and takes approximately 1.5–2 hours round trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Anafonitria Monastery – a 15th-century Venetian tower monastery in the hills above Navagio. This is where Saint Dionysios (the patron saint of Zakynthos) lived as a monk. The peaceful monastery gardens and ancient frescoes offer a spiritual counterpoint to the beach activities. Explore the surrounding pine and olive groves.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a final evening at leisure. Arrange a premium in-suite dining experience or visit the hotel's finest restaurant for a celebratory dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pack a sunrise breakfast hamper from the hotel the night before – coffee in a thermos, fresh pastries, fruit, and yogurt to enjoy at the clifftop viewpoint
meals.lunch: Late lunch at a traditional taverna in Anafonitria village – village salad, grilled lamb chops, roasted potatoes with oregano, and local house wine
meals.dinner: Premium hotel dinner – a celebratory feast: whole roasted suckling pig or slow-cooked lamb shoulder, roasted root vegetables, premium Greek wine, and a dessert platter of traditional sweets: galaktoboureko, baklava, and kataifi

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise hike requires a 05:30 departure for optimal light – the sun rises at approximately 06:00 in late June. Wear sturdy shoes as the clifftop path can be uneven. The Anafonitria Monastery has a strict dress code – shoulders and knees must be covered. Scarves are usually available at the entrance.

day_by_day.morning: Private snorkeling and free-diving experience with a certified local instructor. Explore the underwater world of the Ionian Sea around the Navagio area – sea caves, rocky reefs, and posidonia seagrass meadows teeming with octopus, sea bream, grouper, and starfish. The instructor will teach you free-diving breathing techniques to extend your time underwater.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at the hotel pool with a good book and cold drinks. Enjoy a long, lazy poolside afternoon – your last full relaxation day before departure preparations begin. Arrange any last-minute souvenir shopping or gift wrapping through the hotel concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Penultimate evening dinner – choose your favourite restaurant from the trip for a return visit, or ask the hotel concierge to arrange a special surprise dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast – take your time and enjoy every element of the Greek spread one more time
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch – light and fresh: grilled halloumi skewers, watermelon and feta salad, hummus with warm pita, and a chilled Aperol Spritz
meals.dinner: Return to your favourite restaurant from the trip – or try Akrotiri Restaurant near Cape Skinari for clifftop dining with views of the Kefalonia channel and a menu focused entirely on fresh Ionian seafood

day_by_day.notes: The free-diving session should be booked through the hotel and lasts approximately 3 hours including instruction. No prior experience is necessary. This is also a good evening to begin packing and organising any purchases or gifts to take home.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Navagio Beach – take one last private boat ride down to the Shipwreck Beach for a farewell swim in those impossibly turquoise waters. Spend a quiet hour on the beach, collect a small pebble as a memento, and say goodbye to one of the world's most beautiful beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for checkout and a farewell lunch. Arrange your private transfer to Zakynthos Town or the airport for any final errands. Visit the Zakynthos Town waterfront promenade for a final stroll, gelato, and last-minute shopping for local products: Mandolato nougat, local olive oil, Verdea wine, and handmade ceramics.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Zakynthos Town – a celebratory, unhurried meal at the island's finest restaurant to mark the end of an unforgettable 13-day luxury journey through the Ionian.

meals.breakfast: Farewell hotel breakfast – request a special farewell spread from the hotel chef: a full mezze of all your favourite Greek breakfast items
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at the hotel or a nearby clifftop café – fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, chilled wine, and a dessert of seasonal fresh fruit with Zakynthian honey
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Zakanthi or Malanos in Zakynthos Town – order generously: lobster, fresh fish, premium wines, and every Greek dessert on the menu. Toast to Greece with a glass of Metaxa 12-star brandy

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time is typically 12:00 – arrange a late checkout (14:00) through the hotel concierge if needed. Store your luggage at the hotel while you enjoy your final morning at Navagio. Confirm your departure transfer timing to ensure you arrive at the airport with ample time.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Zakynthos. Enjoy a last Greek coffee and pastry at a café on the Zakynthos Town waterfront, watching the fishing boats come in with the morning catch. Browse the waterfront market one final time if time allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Zakynthos International Airport (Dionysios Solomos Airport). Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for check-in. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of turquoise seas, clifftop sunsets, world-class food, and the unmatched warmth of Greek hospitality.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry the memories of Navagio Beach, the Blue Caves, private yacht days, and exceptional Ionian cuisine with you as you return home.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast at a waterfront café in Zakynthos Town – Freddo cappuccino, fresh tiropita (cheese pie), and a small plate of local honey and yogurt
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a quick bite at a café near the terminal
meals.dinner: Onboard or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Zakynthos International Airport is approximately 6 km from Zakynthos Town and 45–50 minutes from the Navagio Beach area. Confirm your return flight details and ensure all purchased liquids (olive oil, wine) are properly packed in checked luggage. Consider leaving a review and gratuity for exceptional hotel staff. Καλό ταξίδι – Safe travels!
